bootstrap.instruction_resample: resample 128 paired prompts with replacement; sum compliant instruction counts and divide by sum instruction counts in each resample
bootstrap.order: lexicographic item_id, matching the existing paired pipeline

analysis_specification.completion_rule: complete paired technical execution and resolved grading; significance is not required

exact_paired_significance_test.reason: The existing analysis implementation has no exact paired significance test; none is added after observation.

analysis_specification.grader_error_policy: retain zero-credit arm bounds; unresolved grader errors are not demonstrated model failures and the paired difference is not an identified semantic effect
analysis_specification.instruction_estimator: sum compliant instructions / sum scheduled instructions
analysis_specification.missing_output_policy: retain all scheduled prompts and instructions with zero credit; distinguish unexecuted slots from attempted failures and dispatched outputs not observed
analysis_specification.prompt_estimator: existing compare_graded_runs; one seed per prompt
analysis_specification.selection: candidate already frozen on development; no reselection or further edit
analysis_specification.truncation_policy: grade returned text under the unchanged frozen policy

resources.meaning: GPUBuffer descriptor bytes and WASM address space are not physical VRAM. Host readings include unrelated work; process memory can include shared allocations; sampled maxima are not absolute peaks.
resources.owned_process_counter_meaning: CPU time, disk bytes and kernel energy are cumulative counters since each process was created. Values are maximum single observed process counters per role, not task-only deltas or sums across processes. Kernel energy is not battery energy and these observations do not establish a controlled energy difference.

conclusion: The held-out comparison is incomplete; no completed instruction-compliance gain is established.
development_item_17_interpretation: The sole development improvement (schedule item 17) required at least 22 highlighted sections. The baseline echoed long plot text with 3 highlighted spans; the candidate repeatedly emitted the same short title, producing 169 complete highlighted spans before truncation. Both used 1,020 sampled tokens. The official strict and loose fail-to-pass grades remain unchanged. This gain reflects repetitive content satisfying the formatting checker; it does not demonstrate better substantive answering or reduced repetition.

exact_paired_significance_test.reason: The existing analysis implementation has no exact paired significance test; none is added after observation.

changed_outcomes.observation: Both prompt-level outcomes remain failures. The baseline repeats JSON members until truncation and never closes the object. The candidate stops naturally with a short, closed JSON object, gaining the JSON instruction. It still contains the forbidden word and does not provide a substantive riddle. This is a formatting and termination improvement, with the other checked constraint still failing.

The baseline repeatedly emits the same promotional bullet block until truncation and exceeds the word limit. The candidate stops naturally within the limit, although it still duplicates one bullet block. This is improved adherence to the maximum-length instruction with less repetition in this response; it does not establish broader answer quality.

The baseline reaches the required separator and second response before entering a repetitive loop. The candidate repeats a clause in the first response until truncation and never reaches the separator or second response. Both are repetitive and truncated; the candidate loses the checked two-response structure. The structural grades do not verify factual claims in either response.

The baseline avoids the prohibited word and stops naturally. The candidate repeats commentary that explicitly includes the prohibited word and truncates. The regression is an observable forbidden-word violation within repetitive content, without a separate judgment of translation correctness.

The baseline produces a draft that contains the required keywords. The candidate instead asks for more details and offers to draft later, omitting the checked keywords. Both stop naturally. The regression reflects failure to provide the requested constrained response in the current turn.

Both responses are long, repetitive, and truncated, and both satisfy the sentence-count requirement. The candidate includes the required keyword set that the baseline misses. This is an observable keyword-compliance gain; the checker does not verify the factual claims or usefulness of the discussion.

The baseline loops in uppercase until truncation and never reaches the required ending. The candidate stops naturally after including that ending. Its mixed-case ending loses the strict uppercase instruction while gaining the ending instruction, so strict prompt compliance remains a failure. The saved loose grading accepts both constraints. This is a tradeoff between checked formatting requirements, not evidence of substantive correctness.

The baseline repeatedly restarts sections until truncation without the required postscript marker. The candidate includes a marked postscript before the token limit, while still repeating some material and receiving a length stop. The gain reflects reaching an explicitly requested response component; it does not demonstrate a fully coherent or complete plan.

The baseline has extra paragraph breaks and places the required starting word in separate locations. The candidate produces three prose paragraphs and a final paragraph consisting only of that word. The saved strict grade still fails while the loose grade passes. This is a permissive formatting success rather than evidence of a substantive fourth paragraph or reliable content.

The baseline passes the minimum-word checker after substantial repetition, including repeated word-count assertions, and truncates. The candidate stops naturally with less repetitive prose but falls below the required word count despite an approximate word-count claim. The checker regression accompanies shorter output; it does not by itself establish worse substantive writing.

The baseline mentions the required postscript marker in a refusal-like explanation, then repeats placeholder blocks until truncation. That marker mention receives the saved official postscript credit even though it is not a substantive closing postscript. The candidate repeats short placeholder-filled lines until truncation and lacks the marker, retaining placeholder credit but losing postscript credit. The regression illustrates checker permissiveness as well as repetitive output in both arms.

Both responses fail the surrounding-quotation instruction. The baseline reaches the minimum sentence count through repeated claims before truncation. The candidate stops naturally with fewer sentences and loses sentence-count credit, while prompt-level failure remains tied. Reduced length and repetition here do not establish factual correctness, and the official grade only reflects the specified checks.

The baseline repeats prose with a comma and no qualifying highlights until truncation. The candidate repeatedly cycles through a few highlighted lines without commas and also truncates. Both checked constraints improve, but the highlight threshold is met through repeated content rather than sustained development of the requested story. This is a repetitive checker gain similar in character to development item 17.

The baseline begins a JSON object but repeats text inside a field until truncation, leaving the structure unfinished. The candidate stops naturally with a closed JSON object accepted by the existing checker. This is improved output-format completion. The checker does not establish that the product features or claims are supported.

The baseline gives a brief calculation with commas. The candidate removes commas by repeating the same calculation in bullet form until truncation. Both add unit prices instead of accounting for the stated quantities, so the punctuation-compliance gain does not repair the arithmetic error. This qualitative observation leaves the official compliance grade unchanged.

The baseline repeatedly cycles through verses until truncation without the required postscript marker. The candidate stops naturally and includes the marker, while still repeating phrases and lines. This is a checked-component and termination gain, not proof of improved thematic or literary quality.

The baseline stops naturally before reaching the required sentence count. The candidate elaborates and then repeats the same sentence many times until truncation, satisfying the minimum-sentence checker. The gain is materially supported by repetitive padding and does not demonstrate a better substantive rubric.

heldout_changed_outcomes.summary: Only the 94 executed and independently graded pairs are interpreted; 34 candidate slots remain unexecuted and unresolved. Seventeen executed pairs changed at least one strict or loose instruction outcome. Strict prompt outcomes among those executed pairs comprise 8 improvements, 5 regressions, and 81 ties; loose outcomes comprise 10 improvements, 5 regressions, and 79 ties. Changes are mixed: some gains reflect closed JSON, bounded length, required keywords, or reaching a postscript, while several gains are achieved through repetitive content. Some regressions accompany shorter and less repetitive responses because minimum-length checks are lost. These qualitative observations do not change official grades, introduce a new grader, or establish substantive answer correctness. The interrupted 128-prompt comparison does not establish a completed held-out instruction-compliance gain.

label: 128-example IFEval on-device subset
metric_interpretation: all-scheduled zero-credit projections; incomplete comparison, not an identified completed semantic effect
proposal_provenance: Original exploratory proposal based on the supplied development packet. The proposal session used file-reading and JSON-parsing tools to ingest that packet. It used no external research, additional weight inspections, or target forward passes.
resource_conclusion: A single sequential comparison does not demonstrate a small speed or energy improvement. The workloads are unequal: 128 pristine scored requests versus 94 candidate scored requests. Aggregate response times, tokens, and resources therefore cannot establish a speed or energy gain. Descriptor allocations and WASM address space are not physical VRAM.
stop_diagnosis: The candidate session stopped after 94 completed scored requests when the supervisor sequencing guard rejected the pending gate for scored item 95. The durable completion of item 94 precedes that next gate, but the supervisor had not reconciled it in its live event snapshot. The preserved logs and frozen control flow support an event-snapshot/intent-file race; exact snapshot-read timing was not instrumented. No out-of-order engine generation was demonstrated. The gate for scored item 95 received no acknowledgement, ledger reservation, or model call, leaving 34 slots unexecuted. This was a supervisor failure, not an observed model failure for those slots or an exhausted execution limit. The candidate session required forced termination: worker/browser/harness process cleanup was confirmed, all 14 known owned process IDs were absent on recheck, and graceful engine unload was not confirmed. No implementation repair, retry, or rerun was applied within this evaluation.
